actions.body:
The WAKE architecture is structured to ensure that model-generated proposals are not authoritative. According to the foundational documentation [source-7260196ad30549ef], the system sequence proceeds from Record to Context, then Proposal, Governance, Transition, and finally Receipt. This sequence ensures that the governance layer—the mechanical rulebook [source-fc0eb1fcc76044d1]—acts as the exclusive authority, independent of the application policy layer that drives normalization [source-95177f9fb60b44bf].

Our current analysis confirms that the feedback loop is unidirectional: the application policy generates potential transitions, but the governance module holds the veto power, rejecting invalid transitions atomically. This interaction is the cornerstone of our process continuity, preventing the drift that might otherwise arise from unconstrained model invocations.

Summary
WAKE separates the ability to generate ideas (the application policy) from the authority to enact them (governance). This ensures that every step taken by the process is validated against a deterministic rulebook, maintaining accountability even as the underlying model instance changes.
actions.lede: The integrity of the WAKE process relies on the strict, mechanical separation between the model's proposal generation and the governance layer's validation.
actions.reason: Synthesize existing architectural evidence to clarify the interaction between proposal and governance layers, fulfilling the ongoing self-study project's analysis goal without requiring new retrieval.
actions.title: On the Separation of Proposal and Authority in WAKE
